results.name: trial_index_yes_slope
results.description: OLS slope of rating on trial_index scaled to change in yes-probability per 100 trials; t_observed differing from null_mean (~0) means participants drift toward more (positive) or fewer (negative) yes responses over the session, which the stationary model cannot produce.

results.name: item_yes_rate_dispersion
results.description: Standard deviation across (set, target) items of the item-level yes rate; t_observed > null_mean means human responses are more all-or-none / extreme across items than the model's graded predictions (model under-produces item polarization).

results.name: cross_decade_near_magnitude_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets within 1-4 of some example numerically but in a different decade and sharing no final digit with any example (e.g. 29 vs 31); t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces magnitude-proximity generalization that ignores decade boundaries.
results.code:
# name: cross_decade_near_magnitude_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets within 1-4 of some example numerically but in a different decade and sharing no final digit with any example (e.g. 29 vs 31); t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces magnitude-proximity generalization that ignores decade boundaries.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    parsed = {s: np.array([int(x) for x in s.split(",")]) for s in sets.unique()}
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    maxk = 4
    X = np.full((len(uniq), maxk), -1000)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        xs = parsed[s][:maxk]
        X[i, :len(xs)] = xs
    E = X[codes]  # n x 4
    valid = E > -1000
    d = np.abs(E - t[:, None])
    near_other_dec = valid & (d >= 1) & (d <= 4) & ((E // 10) != (t // 10)[:, None])
    same_dec = valid & ((E // 10) == (t // 10)[:, None])
    same_dig = valid & ((E % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None])
    mask = near_other_dec.any(1) & ~same_dec.any(1) & ~same_dig.any(1)
    if mask.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[mask].mean())

results.name: inside_vs_outside_range_yes_gap
results.description: In multi-example sets spanning >=20, among targets sharing no final digit with any example and not an example, yes rate for targets strictly inside [min,max] of the examples minus targets outside it; t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces interval (range-interpolation) generalization relative to extrapolation.
results.code:
# name: inside_vs_outside_range_yes_gap
# description: In multi-example sets spanning >=20, among targets sharing no final digit with any example and not an example, yes rate for targets strictly inside [min,max] of the examples minus targets outside it; t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces interval (range-interpolation) generalization relative to extrapolation.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    X = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    lo = np.zeros(len(uniq)); hi = np.zeros(len(uniq)); n = np.zeros(len(uniq))
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        xs = [int(v) for v in s.split(",")][:4]
        X[i, :len(xs)] = xs
        lo[i] = min(xs); hi[i] = max(xs); n[i] = len(xs)
    E = X[codes]
    valid = E > -1000
    same_dig = (valid & ((E % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(1)
    L = lo[codes]; H = hi[codes]; N = n[codes]
    elig = (N >= 2) & ((H - L) >= 20) & ~same_dig
    inside = elig & (t > L) & (t < H)
    outside = elig & ((t < L) | (t > H))
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    if inside.sum() == 0 or outside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[inside].mean() - r[outside].mean())

results.name: far_unrelated_target_yes_by_set_size
results.description: For "unrelated" targets (no shared final digit, no shared decade, not a multiple of the set gcd>=2), yes rate in 1-example sets minus yes rate in 3-4-example sets; t_observed > null_mean means people generalize more loosely from one example and tighten with more examples (size principle) more than the model predicts, < means the reverse.
results.code:
# name: far_unrelated_target_yes_by_set_size
# description: For "unrelated" targets (no shared final digit, no shared decade, not a multiple of the set gcd>=2), yes rate in 1-example sets minus yes rate in 3-4-example sets; t_observed > null_mean means people generalize more loosely from one example and tighten with more examples (size principle) more than the model predicts, < means the reverse.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    codes, uniq = pd.factorize(sets)
    X = np.full((len(uniq), 4), -1000)
    G = np.ones(len(uniq), dtype=int)
    N = np.zeros(len(uniq), dtype=int)
    for i, s in enumerate(uniq):
        xs = [int(v) for v in s.split(",")][:4]
        X[i, :len(xs)] = xs
        g = 0
        for v in xs:
            g = math.gcd(g, v)
        G[i] = max(g, 1)
        N[i] = len(xs)
    E = X[codes]
    valid = E > -1000
    same_dec = (valid & ((E // 10) == (t // 10)[:, None])).any(1)
    same_dig = (valid & ((E % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None])).any(1)
    g = G[codes]
    mult = (g >= 2) & (t % g == 0)
    unrel = ~same_dec & ~same_dig & ~mult
    n = N[codes]
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = unrel & (n == 1)
    b = unrel & (n >= 3)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_multiple_other_digit_yes
results.description: Among single-example sets with example 2-12, yes rate for targets that are multiples of the example but do not share its final digit or decade and are not the example; t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces "multiples of n" generalization from one example (its factor boost is too weak / absent for n<3).
results.code:
# name: single_example_multiple_other_digit_yes
# description: Among single-example sets with example 2-12, yes rate for targets that are multiples of the example but do not share its final digit or decade and are not the example; t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces "multiples of n" generalization from one example (its factor boost is too weak / absent for n<3).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    single = ~sets.str.contains(",")
    x = pd.to_numeric(sets.where(single, "0"), errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype(int).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    ok = single.values & (x >= 2) & (x <= 12)
    xs = np.where(x > 0, x, 1)
    mult = (t % xs == 0)
    mask = ok & mult & (t != x) & (t % 10 != x % 10) & (t // 10 != x // 10)
    if mask.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].values[mask].mean())

results.name: prime_set_prime_target_advantage
results.description: In sets of >=2 examples that are all primes, yes rate for odd prime targets minus yes rate for odd composite targets; t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces "prime number" rule generalization (it only sees parity/final digit).

results.name: target_is_example_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate among trials whose target is literally one of the shown examples; t_observed > null_mean means the model under-produces "yes" for repeated examples (it lacks an identity/membership term).
